description: Two documentation-only architecture diagrams for the car-search service: (1) the current agentic request flow (Mermaid + draw.io XML), and (2) the target AWS production deployment centered on API Gateway + Bedrock AgentCore Runtime/Gateway + Lambda + S3 (draw.io XML with official AWS icons, Miro-importable). No application code or infrastructure changes.

userStories.title: Agentic flow diagram (Mermaid)
userStories.description: As an engineer, I want a Mermaid diagram of the current agentic request flow so I can read/review it directly in the repo's markdown docs without opening another tool.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at docs/diagrams/agentic-flow.mmd, starting with a valid Mermaid diagram declaration (flowchart or sequenceDiagram)

Diagram includes every step in the real flow, each as a labeled node/participant: client request, POST /search, filter extraction (Strands agent, structured output), guardrail fallbacks (synonym mapping + price-shorthand normalization), contradiction detection, clarify-trigger check, clarify sub-agent, search_listings/search_full_dataset (DuckDB over data/*.parquet), zero-result auto-relaxation loop, deterministic ranking/cap, explanation generation, response

The order of steps matches src/car_search/orchestrator.py::run_search exactly: extract -> contradiction check -> clarify-trigger check -> (clarify short-circuit OR relax_and_search -> rank_and_cap -> build_explanation)

The two LLM-calling steps (filter extraction, clarify sub-agent) are visually distinguished from the deterministic steps via a Mermaid classDef/class applied consistently (e.g. one class for LLM-backed nodes, one for deterministic nodes)
The clarify short-circuit path is drawn as a distinct path that leads directly to the response node, never passing through search_listings/search_full_dataset
A short legend (2-4 sentences) explaining the color/style distinction is included, either as a comment block at the top of agentic-flow.mmd or in an accompanying docs/diagrams/agentic-flow.md
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: docs/diagrams/agentic-flow.mmd (Mermaid flowchart) + docs/diagrams/agentic-flow.md (legend). Matches src/car_search/orchestrator.py::run_search step-for-step, verified by grepping every function name (extract_filters, apply_synonym_fallback, detect_contradiction, needs_clarification, ask_clarifying_question, search_full_dataset, relaxation fields, rank_and_cap, build_explanation). LLM-vs-deterministic distinction via classDef llm/deterministic; clarify short-circuit drawn as a separate branch that never reaches search_full_dataset. Rendered and visually verified via a published Artifact (native Mermaid rendering) -- clean, no overlaps.

userStories.title: Agentic flow diagram (draw.io/diagrams.net XML)
userStories.description: As an engineer, I want the same agentic flow available as an editable draw.io diagram so it can be dropped into other tools (Confluence, Miro, slides) without redrawing it.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at docs/diagrams/agentic-flow.drawio
File is well-formed XML (validates with `xmllint --noout` or an equivalent XML parser) with a root <mxfile> element containing an <mxGraphModel>/<root> with mxCell shapes
Contains the same set of steps/nodes as docs/diagrams/agentic-flow.mmd (US-001), findable by label text on the mxCell shapes, in the same order

LLM-calling steps (filter extraction, clarify sub-agent) and deterministic steps use visually distinct mxCell styles (different fillColor/strokeColor), matching the same LLM-vs-deterministic distinction as US-001
The clarify short-circuit path is drawn as a distinct edge path from the main search path, matching US-001
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: docs/diagrams/agentic-flow.drawio -- same step set/order as US-001 (verified via grep of the same function-name keywords), same amber(#fef3c7/#d97706)/blue(#dbeafe/#2563eb) LLM-vs-deterministic distinction, same clarify short-circuit branch. Verified well-formed via `xmllint --noout` (passes).

userStories.title: AWS production deployment diagram (draw.io XML, AWS icons, Miro-ready)
userStories.description: As an engineer, I want a high-level AWS production architecture diagram using official AWS icons so I can import it into Miro and discuss the deployment plan with the team.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at docs/diagrams/aws-production-deployment.drawio
File is well-formed XML (validates with `xmllint --noout` or an equivalent XML parser)

Every AWS service node's mxCell style attribute references an AWS icon shape (style string containing 'mxgraph.aws4.' or 'mxgraph.aws3.'), not a generic rectangle -- verified by grepping the file for these style prefixes, one per required service

Includes distinct, labeled nodes for exactly these components: Client, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, AWS Lambda (labeled as hosting the search_listings tool), Amazon S3 (labeled as holding data/*.parquet), Amazon Bedrock (labeled as the foundation model), Amazon CloudWatch

Edges/arrows connect: Client -> API Gateway -> AgentCore Runtime; AgentCore Runtime -> Bedrock (model calls); AgentCore Runtime -> AgentCore Gateway -> Lambda -> S3 (tool call path); every component has an edge (or clearly grouped connection) to CloudWatch for logs/metrics
No VPC, subnet, security-group, IAM-role, or CI/CD-pipeline shapes are present -- high-level only
A short legend/caption explaining each component's role in one line is included, either as on-canvas text nodes or in an accompanying docs/diagrams/aws-production-deployment.md
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Acceptance criteria intentionally exclude the PRD's manual 'imported into Miro and verified' check -- that requires an actual Miro account/UI and cannot be autonomously verified. A human should do that check once this story's automated criteria pass. docs/diagrams/aws-production-deployment.drawio + docs/diagrams/aws-production-deployment.md (legend). Uses real AWS4 icon shapes sourced from draw.io's actual bundled stencil/sidebar source (mxgraph.aws4.api_gateway, .bedrock_agentcore x2, .bedrock, .lambda, .s3, .cloudwatch_2 -- 7/7 required nodes verified via grep) with correct official per-category colors (Networking #E7157B, AI/ML #01A88D, Compute #ED7100, Storage #7AA116). All 7 required edges present (client->apigw->runtime->bedrock, runtime->gateway->lambda->s3, group->cloudwatch). No VPC/subnet/IAM/security-group shapes (grep confirms 0 matches). Well-formed per `xmllint --noout`. Note: draw.io's AWS icon library has only one 'Bedrock AgentCore' icon (no separate Runtime/Gateway icons yet) -- both nodes reuse it, distinguished by label + a dashed account-boundary grouping; documented in the legend. Manual Miro-import verification (the one PRD check Ralph can't do autonomously) still needed from a human.
